title: IEC 61000-6-3 EMC Emissions Testing India
description: IEC 61000-6-3 EMC testing in India for residential electrical and electronic equipment. Test conducted and radiated emissions with ITC India testing support.

sections.heading: Overview
paragraphs: Electrical and electronic equipment can generate electromagnetic disturbances that interfere with radio reception, communication systems and nearby products. IEC 61000-6-3 is a generic electromagnetic compatibility emission standard used for equipment intended for residential locations when no more specific product or product-family EMC emission standard applies.

ITC India provides IEC 61000-6-3 EMC testing in India for manufacturers and product developers who need to evaluate conducted and radiated emissions before certification, export or market launch. The current IEC 61000-6-3:2026 edition covers equipment for residential locations and can also apply in other locations when the equipment does not fall within IEC 61000-6-8 or IEC 61000-6-4.
Manufacturers requiring broader electromagnetic compatibility support can also review ITC India’s EMC Testing services.

sections.heading: What Does IEC 61000-6-3 Cover?
paragraphs: IEC 61000-6-3 is used when a dedicated product or product-family emission standard has not been published for the equipment.

It is primarily intended for electrical and electronic equipment used in residential locations. It can also cover equipment used in commercial and light-industrial locations that does not meet the professional-equipment conditions addressed by IEC 61000-6-8. Equipment intended for industrial environments may instead fall under IEC 61000-6-4.
Because EMC requirements depend on intended use, installation environment, ports and product category, the correct emission standard should be confirmed before testing.

sections.heading: Conducted and Radiated Emissions
paragraphs: Conducted emissions are electromagnetic disturbances transferred from equipment onto connected cables, particularly power and other applicable wired interfaces. Excessive disturbances can propagate through connected networks and interfere with nearby equipment.
Radiated emissions are disturbances emitted through space from the enclosure, cables and internal circuitry. Testing evaluates whether these emissions remain below the applicable limits.

sections.heading: IEC 61000-6-3 vs IEC 61000-6-1
paragraphs: IEC 61000-6-3 covers emissions: electromagnetic disturbances produced by the equipment. IEC 61000-6-1 covers immunity: the equipment’s ability to continue operating when exposed to disturbances such as electrostatic discharge, RF fields, electrical fast transients and surges.

Products for residential, commercial or light-industrial use may therefore need both emission and immunity evaluation. Manufacturers can review ITC India’s IEC 61000-6-1 EMC Immunity Testing service when a complete generic EMC programme is required.

sections.heading: IEC 61000-6-3, IEC 61000-6-8 and IEC 61000-6-4
paragraphs: Correct environment classification is important. IEC 61000-6-3 is the generic emission standard for residential locations and can also apply where IEC 61000-6-8 or IEC 61000-6-4 does not apply.

IEC 61000-6-8 addresses certain professional equipment for commercial and light-industrial locations that is professionally installed and maintained and is not intended for residential use. IEC 61000-6-4 addresses industrial environments.

sections.heading: Documents Required for Testing
paragraphs: Manufacturers should provide product specifications, rated voltage and frequency, power-supply details, interface and cable information, intended operating modes, product configuration and destination market.
Samples should be supplied with the accessories, cables and external power supplies needed to reproduce normal and worst-case operating conditions during EMC testing.

sections.heading: IEC 61000-6-3 Testing with ITC India
paragraphs: ITC India supports manufacturers with EMC emission testing for electrical and electronic products against applicable IEC, EN and CISPR requirements.
Manufacturers can also review ITC India’s Electrical Equipment Testing Services where EMC forms part of a wider product-compliance programme.
For IEC 61000-6-3 EMC emissions testing in India, submit your product details, required standard edition and technical information through the ITC India testing inquiry form.

sections.heading: What is IEC 61000-6-3?
paragraphs: IEC 61000-6-3 is a generic EMC emission standard for electrical and electronic equipment intended primarily for residential locations where no applicable dedicated product or product-family emission standard exists.

sections.heading: What is the current edition of IEC 61000-6-3?
paragraphs: IEC currently lists IEC 61000-6-3:2026 as the latest edition. Manufacturers should still confirm the edition required by the destination market or certification scheme.

sections.heading: Does IEC 61000-6-3 include immunity testing?
paragraphs: No. IEC 61000-6-3 covers emissions. Generic immunity requirements for residential, commercial and light-industrial environments are addressed by IEC 61000-6-1.

sections.heading: What is the difference between IEC 61000-6-3 and IEC 61000-6-4?
paragraphs: IEC 61000-6-3 is intended primarily for residential locations, while IEC 61000-6-4 applies to industrial environments when no more specific product or product-family standard applies.

sections.heading: Does IEC 61000-6-3 cover commercial and light-industrial equipment?
paragraphs: It can. The 2026 scope works alongside IEC 61000-6-8 so that residential, commercial and light-industrial equipment is covered by the appropriate generic standard.

sections.heading: Can ITC India perform IEC 61000-6-3 EMC testing?
paragraphs: ITC India provides EMC testing support for applicable electrical and electronic equipment. The final scope depends on product type, ports, intended environment, operating modes and required standard edition.
